meta.title: Tree View
meta.description: Recursive hierarchical data with expand/collapse, multi-select, full keyboard navigation, and optional connecting lines. File explorers, org charts, category trees.

blocks.content: Hierarchical data is everywhere — file explorers, org charts, category trees, settings navigation, comment threads. The hard part is never the rendering. The hard part is keyboard navigation: arrow keys that traverse the visible tree, expand collapsed nodes, jump to parents, and skip disabled items. Most implementations skip it entirely.

TreeRoot builds a flat list of visible nodes on every render and maps keyboard events to the correct node — next, previous, parent, first child. AnimatePresence handles expand/collapse. Multi-select works with ⌘/Ctrl click and Shift. The consumer provides nodes and gets selected ids back.

blocks.title: Keyboard navigation is wired automatically
blocks.content: Focus the tree container (click or Tab to it) and all keyboard shortcuts work immediately. No wiring needed. Arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Home/End jump to bounds.
Click any node to select it. Hold ⌘ or Ctrl to multi-select. Click an arrow or folder to expand. Focus the tree and use keyboard navigation.

optionalSteps.title: Peer dependency
optionalSteps.note: Required for smooth animated node expansion.

blocks.content: Pass nodes to TreeRoot. Each node has an id, label, and optional icon and children. The tree is uncontrolled by default — pass defaultExpanded and defaultSelected in config for initial state.
Focus the tree container by clicking or tabbing to it. All navigation runs on the visible flat list — collapsed branches are skipped.

blocks.content: Enable multi-select by passing multiSelect: true in config. ⌘/Ctrl+click adds or removes a node from the selection. Without multiSelect, clicking a node replaces the current selection.

blocks.code:
<TreeRoot
  nodes={nodes}
  config={{ multiSelect: true }}
  onSelect={(ids, nodes) => {
    console.log("selected ids:", ids);
  }}
/>

blocks.content: Pass showLines: true to render faint vertical lines connecting sibling nodes. Useful for deep trees where indentation alone doesn't communicate structure clearly.

items.q: How does keyboard navigation work across deep or nested branches?
items.a: Tree View flattens all visible nodes dynamically into a single linear focus array. Arrow keys move smoothly through visible nodes while automatically respecting expand/collapse state.

items.q: Can I render custom icons for specific file extensions or folder types?
items.a: Yes! Pass any React component or Tabler icon to the icon prop of each TreeNode definition.
